consumption.n: Atlas estimate: apparent consumption of primary aluminium in 2024, by country: production plus imports minus exports of the same product and year, in kt. Production: primary aluminium smelter production (USGS), USGS MCS 2026 2024 column. Imports and exports: CEPII BACI 2024, unwrought aluminium (HS 7601), gross weight, with the atlas's cleaning rules. Trade is unwrought aluminium, alloyed or not (HS 7601), which includes alloys made from scrap; production is primary smelter output only. The result is smelter output plus net trade in unwrought metal, not the use of primary metal alone. Stock changes are not known, so this is apparent consumption, not measured use. Only the countries for which USGS gives production are listed (12); 0 of them are left out because one of the three terms is missing, and 2 because the result is negative (Iceland, United Arab Emirates). A country that trades the product but has no USGS production figure has no production term and is not in the table. World: the world production of the same product in 2024 as USGS gives it (72,800 kt, the sum of its countries and its 'Other countries' line): trade nets out in the world, so apparent consumption of the world is its production apart from changes in stocks, which are not known. The shares and 'Rest of world' (the countries not listed, dropped ones included) are computed on it; the order of the rows is not a world ranking.

notes: Trade is unwrought aluminium (HS 7601); USGS production is primary smelter output. Bauxite reserves are under 'bauxite'.

Unwrought aluminium (HS 7601) from the United States to Malaysia: 0.536 Mt in 2024 (CEPII BACI), declared at 1,034 USD per tonne, 40% of the tonne-weighted median of the group (2,565); the 2024 average aluminium price is 2,419 USD per tonne (World Bank Pink Sheet), and the pair is declared at 43% of it. Material priced like scrap or alloy, or another cheaper product, declared under this code is a plausible cause; it is not established here.

Unwrought aluminium is two customs codes of nearly equal weight in 2024: HS 760110, not alloyed, 15.0 Mt, and HS 760120, alloys, 15.4 Mt. Each pair of the main tables is split between them in proportion to the six-digit rows of the same pair (CEPII BACI); alloys include ingot made from scrap, so the second code is where recycled metal is traded.
